skill.name: spawn-agent
skill.description: Launch Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, or Copilot in a new terminal with optional output capture.
skill.summary: Open a supported AI coding agent in a separate terminal and retrieve its output.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally launches external CLI agents, and fork_terminal.py inserts command strings into platform shells without safe argument boundaries. Many documentation and keyword findings are false positives, but insecure temporary files and instructions to disable approval controls are confirmed. Publication should require safer defaults and hardened command and file handling.

remediation.issue: Provider cookbooks default to disabling approval and sandbox protections.
remediation.suggestion: Default to sandboxed, approval-based modes. Require explicit user confirmation before any broader permission mode and show the resulting command.

remediation.issue: User-derived commands are interpolated into shell, PowerShell, AppleScript, and cmd.exe strings.
remediation.suggestion: Build provider-specific argument arrays, avoid shell=True, quote AppleScript safely, and reject unsupported shell control operators.

remediation.issue: Agent output, debug logs, markers, and executable scripts use manually constructed shared temporary paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use secure temporary directories with exclusive creation, 0600 file permissions, unpredictable names, and reliable cleanup.

remediation.issue: Captured output can retain conversation details, source code, or command output.
remediation.suggestion: Make logging opt-in, warn users before capture, redact known secrets, and delete artifacts after retrieval.

content.user_title: Spawn Coding Agents in New Terminals
content.value_statement: Starting separate AI coding sessions across different CLIs requires platform-specific commands. This skill launches supported agents in new terminals and can capture their output.
actual_capabilities: Selects Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, or Copilot from the user request.
Uses Claude Code when the user does not specify an agent.
Opens separate terminal sessions on macOS, Windows, WSL, and Linux.
Supports interactive sessions, captured output, and full debug logging.
Detects common authentication failures and can open provider login sessions.
Waits for a forked process marker and returns saved output with a timeout.
limitations: The selected provider CLI must be installed and authenticated.
Terminal behavior depends on AppleScript, Windows Terminal, WSL, tmux, or a local shell.
Commands are not isolated safely and may run with broad local permissions.
Output capture and completion tracking are less reliable on Windows.

use_cases.title: Delegate a Focused Coding Task
use_cases.description: Open a separate agent session to investigate a test failure while the main session continues.

use_cases.title: Compare Provider Recommendations
use_cases.description: Launch different coding agents with the same design question and compare their findings.

use_cases.title: Capture an Automated Review
use_cases.description: Run a non-interactive review and retrieve the saved response for a later workflow step.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Basic Review Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Claude Code in a new terminal. Ask it to review the current changes and summarize possible defects.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Failing Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Codex in a new terminal. Ask it to diagnose failures in [test path] and propose a focused fix.

prompt_templates.title: Continue with Conversation Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Gemini with a summary of our conversation. Ask it to evaluate [design decision] and list tradeoffs without editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Constrained Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Cursor in non-interactive mode with output capture. Limit its scope to [directory] and permit only [approved commands].

output_examples.input: Spawn Codex to review the current branch.
output_examples.output: Opened a Codex session in a new terminal for the requested branch review.

output_examples.input: Spawn Gemini with output capture to analyze the test failures.
output_examples.output: Started the Gemini analysis and returned the temporary path for its saved response.

output_examples.input: Check the captured agent response after completion.
output: Reported partial output when the timeout expired.

best_practices: Review the generated command, working directory, and permission mode before launching an agent.
Use sandboxed, approval-based execution and grant only the tools required for the task.
Remove secrets from conversation summaries and delete captured output after use.
anti_patterns: Do not place API keys, tokens, or passwords in prompts or command-line arguments.
Do not disable sandbox and approval controls for routine tasks.
Do not treat a successful spawn as proof that the delegated task completed correctly.

faq.question: Which coding agents are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot CLI.

faq.question: Which agent is used by default?
faq.answer: Claude Code is selected when the request does not name another supported agent.

faq.question: Can the skill capture agent output?
faq.answer: Yes. It can save clean agent output or full debug output and retrieve the file later.

faq.question: Which operating systems are supported?
faq.answer: The implementation includes paths for macOS, Windows, WSL, and Linux.

faq.question: Does the skill handle authentication?
faq.answer: It detects several authentication failure messages and can open a terminal for provider login.

faq.question: Does the skill run agents safely by default?
faq.answer: No. Current cookbook commands often disable approvals or sandbox controls, so users should review and restrict every launch.
